projects.title: Engineering Orchestrator
projects.oneLine: A multi-agent operating layer connecting requirements, PLM, design, simulation, and downstream lifecycle workflows.
projects.problem: Engineering work spans specialized tools, fragmented knowledge, and lifecycle hand-offs. A useful AI layer has to coordinate these systems without hiding ownership or process constraints.
projects.ownership: Architecture and delivery leadership across agent responsibilities, tool boundaries, retrieval patterns, and alignment with engineering stakeholders.
approach: Decompose lifecycle work into bounded agent responsibilities.
Connect enterprise knowledge and engineering tools through explicit retrieval and tool contracts.
Keep validation and human decision points visible in the workflow.
decisions: Prefer orchestrated specialist agents over one general-purpose prompt.
Treat tool access and knowledge retrieval as separate, observable concerns.
Design for reusable process patterns rather than a single demonstration.
impact: Created a cohesive AI-assisted layer across previously separate lifecycle activities.
Established reusable orchestration patterns for additional engineering use cases.
lessons: Agent boundaries are most useful when they match real process ownership.
Adoption depends as much on validation and transparency as model capability.
projects.confidentiality: Public description is intentionally generalized. Client names, internal architecture, proprietary data, and operational metrics are excluded.

projects.title: FMEA Analysis Agents
projects.oneLine: End-to-end agents supporting workflow decomposition, context retrieval, analysis guidance, validation, and structured FMEA outputs.
projects.problem: FMEA analysis requires structured reasoning, domain context, repeatable outputs, and accountable expert review rather than free-form text generation.
projects.ownership: Development lead for workflow decomposition, agent responsibilities, prompt and tool design, validation strategy, and team delivery.
approach: Represent analysis as explicit stages with bounded inputs and outputs.
Retrieve supporting context before analysis and preserve structured results.
Place validation and expert review at consequential transitions.
decisions: Use graph orchestration for inspectable state transitions.
Separate context retrieval, analysis guidance, and validation.
Optimize for traceable structured output rather than conversational fluency.
impact: Made an expert workflow more consistent and easier to inspect.
Created a repeatable foundation for adjacent quality-analysis use cases.
lessons: Quality workflows need explicit uncertainty and review states.
Structured intermediate outputs make agent behavior easier to validate.
projects.confidentiality: The workflow description is generalized and excludes proprietary failure data, prompts, integrations, and evaluation results.

projects.title: Requirements Engineering Agents
projects.oneLine: Agents assisting requirements elicitation, analysis, interpretation, management, and traceability-oriented work.
projects.problem: Requirements work combines large context, ambiguity, domain rules, and traceability obligations that cannot be handled reliably by isolated prompts.
projects.ownership: Lead delivery of the agent workflow and coordinate technical implementation with engineering process expectations.
approach: Break the workflow into elicitation, analysis, interpretation, and management tasks.
Give agents scoped tools and context appropriate to each responsibility.
Preserve links between source context, analysis, and resulting requirements.
decisions: Use a deep-agent pattern for longer-running, multi-step work.
Make traceability a first-class output.
Keep requirements specialists in the review loop.
impact: Improved access to process guidance during requirements work.
Created a reusable agent pattern for traceability-oriented workflows.
lessons: Good requirements agents clarify ambiguity; they should not silently resolve it.
Traceability must be designed into the workflow rather than added at the end.
projects.confidentiality: Examples, source requirements, prompts, and enterprise integrations are not published.

projects.title: Non-Conformity Agents
projects.oneLine: Quality-workflow agents helping engineers navigate context, evidence, and process-driven next actions.
projects.problem: Non-conformity work requires engineers to connect issue context, supporting evidence, and prescribed process steps across fragmented information.
projects.ownership: Built the agent workflow and retrieval behavior around practical quality-process needs.
approach: Retrieve relevant issue and process context.
Organize evidence before proposing next actions.
Keep the engineer responsible for disposition and approval.
decisions: Ground suggestions in retrieved evidence.
Separate evidence summarization from recommended actions.
Avoid autonomous decisions in consequential quality steps.
impact: Made quality context and process guidance easier to navigate.
Reduced friction in identifying evidence and appropriate next steps.
lessons: Evidence provenance is essential in quality workflows.
A useful assistant narrows the search space without replacing accountable decisions.
projects.confidentiality: No product, defect, customer, or internal quality-system data is included.

projects.title: FEM Copilot
projects.oneLine: A context-aware assistant for model creation, boundary conditions, material selection, and finite-element analysis steps.
projects.problem: Finite-element workflows require many context-dependent setup decisions and repeated navigation between modelling practice, material data, and analysis steps.
projects.ownership: Shaped a copilot concept combining engineering context with workflow-oriented guidance.
approach: Provide step-aware suggestions rather than generic simulation answers.
Connect recommendations to modelling context and analysis stage.
Keep engineering assumptions visible for review.
decisions: Use a copilot pattern instead of autonomous model creation.
Surface assumptions alongside recommendations.
Prioritize workflow guidance and consistency.
impact: Made domain guidance available closer to the modelling workflow.
Demonstrated how GenAI can complement established simulation automation.
lessons: Engineering copilots need domain context more than broad conversational ability.
Visible assumptions are critical when suggestions affect analysis quality.
projects.confidentiality: No proprietary models, solver inputs, material data, or customer results are shown.

projects.title: Chassis Automation Tool
projects.oneLine: Interactive and batch automation for CAD organization, mesh creation, seam weld creation, and engineering quality checks.
projects.problem: Chassis pre-processing contains repetitive, quality-sensitive steps that consume engineering time and vary when executed manually.
projects.ownership: Designed and delivered interactive and batch automation covering core preprocessing tasks and quality checks.
approach: Translate engineering work instructions into repeatable automation stages.
Support both guided interactive use and batch processing.
Embed quality checks close to the automated operation.
decisions: Preserve interactive control where engineering judgement is needed.
Use batch execution for repeatable high-volume steps.
Treat quality checks as part of the workflow, not a final afterthought.
impact: Improved workflow consistency and reinforced engineering quality standards.
lessons: Successful automation begins with a precise understanding of the manual workflow.
Reusable templates and checks are as important as execution speed.
projects.confidentiality: The manufacturer, vehicle data, internal scripts, and measured time savings are confidential.

projects.title: Alloy Wheel DVP Automation
projects.oneLine: An end-to-end wheel-simulation pipeline spanning pre-processing, analysis preparation, post-processing, and automated report generation.
projects.problem: Wheel simulation required repeated modelling, setup, review, and reporting steps, creating avoidable effort and variation across the design-validation workflow.
projects.ownership: Developed an end-to-end automation tool that guided the wheel workflow from pre-processing through report generation.
approach: Reduce the workflow to the minimum inputs required from the engineer.
Automate repeatable pre-processing and post-processing stages.
Generate reports in HyperView through Altair report APIs.
decisions: Automate the full DVP path instead of isolated modelling commands.
Keep user inputs small and explicit.
Use supported report APIs rather than manual slide assembly.
impact: Improved wheel-modelling efficiency through end-to-end automation.
Made report generation faster and more consistent.
lessons: The largest gains often come from connecting pre-processing and reporting into one workflow.
Minimal-input automation depends on carefully defined defaults and validation.
projects.confidentiality: The manufacturer, wheel models, simulation criteria, internal scripts, and measured time savings are excluded.

projects.title: Abaqus ODB Compression Tool
projects.oneLine: A standalone Python utility that reduced large Abaqus ODB result files by approximately 90% through selective variable and frame extraction.
projects.problem: Large Abaqus ODB files were slow to download from compute clusters and expensive to inspect when invariant calculations had to be performed repeatedly.
projects.ownership: Built a standalone Python compression tool for engineering teams working with large simulation-result files.
approach: Let users select only the result variables and frames needed for downstream review.
Write a reduced ODB rather than moving the entire source result set.
Preserve flexibility for different post-processing needs.
decisions: Use selective extraction instead of generic file compression.
Keep the utility standalone so it could fit existing engineering workflows.
Expose variable and frame selection to the user.
impact: Achieved an approximately 90% compression ratio on large ODB files.
Reduced cluster-download time and improved plotting performance by avoiding unnecessary invariant calculations.
lessons: Engineering-data performance often improves most by removing unneeded domain data, not merely compressing bytes.
User-controlled selection made the utility reusable across analysis types.
projects.confidentiality: No customer ODB files, simulation results, model details, or proprietary scripts are published.

projects.title: Google Slides Report Automation
projects.oneLine: A form-driven Google Apps Script workflow that assembled engineering reports from uploaded images using a predefined Slides template.
projects.problem: Engineering teams repeatedly assembled image-heavy reports by hand, even when the structure and presentation template were already known.
projects.ownership: Created the report-generation script, predefined Slides template, and upload form used to trigger the workflow.
approach: Collect report images and inputs through a simple form.
Map submitted content into a controlled Google Slides template.
Trigger report creation automatically after submission.
decisions: Use a familiar form instead of exposing scripting controls.
Separate the reusable presentation template from report content.
Standardize structure while keeping input collection lightweight.
impact: Improved consistency across recurring engineering reports.
lessons: Small workflow automations can remove substantial coordination overhead.
Templates turn document generation into a maintainable system rather than a one-off script.
projects.confidentiality: The original template, uploaded engineering images, report contents, and organization details are not included.

sourceSections.title: Profile
sourceSections.content: I am an Agentic AI Engineer and Senior Analyst at Accenture DACH based in Munich with 10+ years across CAE automation, engineering digitization, and enterprise delivery. I architect multi-agent workflows that combine retrieval, tools, validation, and human review across PLM, requirements, quality, and simulation. My experience includes Python, LangChain, LangGraph, Deep Agents, Google ADK, LLM orchestration, RAG, vector databases for embedding storage and similarity search, MCP-enabled integration, Azure AI Foundry, Azure DevOps, Azure Portal, GCP, agile delivery, and stakeholder alignment.

sourceSections.title: Skills and capabilities
sourceSections.content: I have worked with vector databases in RAG implementations, using them for embedding storage and similarity search. My other Agentic AI skills include multi-agent orchestration, LangChain, LangGraph, Deep Agents, Google ADK, Model Context Protocol (MCP), LLM orchestration, prompt and workflow design, AI copilots, and human review patterns. My cloud and delivery skills include Azure AI Foundry, Azure DevOps, Azure Portal, and Google Cloud Platform (GCP). I use Python and Tcl/Tk for engineering automation, and Cursor AI, OpenAI Codex, and Claude Code for AI-assisted development. My engineering-domain capabilities cover requirements engineering, PLM, FMEA and quality, CAE, FEM, simulation automation, and engineering reporting. The public portfolio does not assign a proficiency or confidence level to database skills and does not identify a specific vector database product.

sourceSections.title: Career progression
sourceSections.content: I have worked at Accenture DACH, Altair Engineering, ZF Friedrichshafen, Valeo, and Tata Consultancy Services. My progression moves from CAE and FEM automation through reusable engineering platforms to enterprise agentic AI systems.

sourceSections.title: Selected work
sourceSections.content: The portfolio contains five Agentic AI or GenAI systems: the Engineering Orchestrator coordinates agents across engineering lifecycle workflows; FMEA Analysis Agents structure quality analysis and expert review; Requirements Engineering Agents support elicitation, analysis, management, and traceability; Non-Conformity Agents retrieve quality evidence and guide process-driven next actions; and the FEM Copilot provides context-aware simulation guidance. The portfolio also contains four traditional engineering automation systems—Chassis Automation, Alloy Wheel DVP Automation, Abaqus ODB Compression, and Google Slides Report Automation—which must not be described as Agentic AI systems.

sourceSections.content: I architect an Engineering Orchestrator connecting requirements, PLM, design, simulation, and lifecycle activities through bounded agents, explicit tool access, and RAG backed by vector databases for embedding storage and similarity search, with validation and visible human decision points.

sourceSections.title: Chassis Automation Tool
